column1: # Private pre-push host table for omnibase_infra (OMN-17232).
# THIS FILE IS AUTHORITY FOR HOST IDENTITY. It holds every lab row that used to
# ship in omnibase_infra scripts/hooks/prepush_hosts.tsv and in the placement overlay
# config/lab/prepush_hosts.omnibase_infra.overlay.tsv (retired). A deployment's hosts,
# addresses, logins, paths, slots and tiers are deployment facts supplied by
# whoever runs the system, so they live here and not in the shipped repository;
# the shipped file keeps the column schema and one disabled localhost row.
# The hook reads this file through the workspace-config resolver:
# ${ONEX_WORKSPACE_CONFIG_ROOT:-$registry_root/../ops_tooling_pkg}/config/onex/overlays/prepush_hosts/prepush_hosts.omnibase_infra.tsv
# and appends its rows to the shipped table's. When the root is a git checkout the
# hook reads the COMMITTED copy (`git show HEAD:`) and refuses if the working tree
# differs, so an uncommitted row cannot self-designate a machine as an authorizing
# gate host. The remote leg ships the verified rows to the target host beside the
# bundle, so the conftest guard there reads the same table.
# The column schema, the meaning of each column and the procedure for adding a
# host are documented in the header of omnibase_infra scripts/hooks/prepush_hosts.tsv.
# Adding, moving or resizing a host is an edit to THIS file, never to that one.
#label

lab-host-a Linux host, 32 cores. OMN-16989 denial for omnibase_infra LIFTED: all 15 'host-coupled' failures were measured in the lab-host-a gate-runner CONTAINER, not on this host over the remote leg. Re-measured 2026-08-30 over the real leg: tests/unit/ 24930 green in 669s, tests/ci/ 1892 green in 122s, both host_mode=authorizing pytest_exit=0. Separately PROVEN-CAPABLE for omnibase_core heavy escalations -- measured 2026-08-30 by parsing ~/push-lanes/queue-runner.log, not assumed: 12 completed heavy omnibase_core lanes span 2h43m20s (OMN-13902-main) to 3h48m55s (OMN-16581), 9 of them rc=0. So a core full suite costing ~10h on an M1 Air (OMN-16998) finishes here in under 4h. Reachable only by HAND-ROUTING a lane into that queue (~/push-lanes/lanes/<lane>.env + QUEUE): omnibase_core has no OMN-16991 dispatch seam of its own -- that gap is OMN-17159. slots=1 (OMN-17269) -- this row runs the separate ~/push-lanes/QUEUE serializer, a different concurrency mechanism; widening it is out of scope here OMN-17485: heavy_local flipped allowed -> prefer_remote and placement_tier set last_resort -- this host is the dev runtime lane's live evidence surface (the OMN-16963 AC5 delegation_workflow_state terminalization measurement reads from it) AND an interactive collaborator workspace (OMN-17143 lane), and on 2026-09-01 its gate-runner slot ran heavy suites back-to-back 08:31Z-12:02Z while a collaborator's own governed full core suite (44464 tests, 2h58m) ran host-side concurrently. A heavy escalation ORIGINATING here now attempts lab placement first (same OMN-17392 semantics as h906), and as a TARGET this row is taken only when no default-tier host is fit. OMN-17743: slots=1 -> 3. Sized from live measurement 2026-09-03T10:57Z-11:03Z, not from the declared reservations -- summing HostConfig.NanoCpus over all 147 running containers gives 205.80 CPUs on a 32-core box (6.4x oversubscribed; 182.00 of it the 90-runner fleet at 2 CPUs each, 28 containers capped at nothing), which is 84x actual consumption and therefore useless for sizing. What was measured instead: `docker stats --no-stream` over those same 147 containers totals 245.7% = 2.46 cores, of which the 90 CI runners are 11.2% = 0.11 cores (idle since trusted CI moved to GitHub-hosted runners, OMN-16688) and the 57 non-runner containers -- five runtime lanes, brokers, ai-sglang at 101.21% -- are 234.5% = 2.34 cores; /proc/loadavg sampled 5x/4s read 7.36 7.01 7.01 6.93 6.86 (mean load1 7.03/32 = 0.22x) with exactly one heavy leg in flight at 98.7% ~= 1.0 core, so the non-prepush baseline is ~6.0 of 32 cores. Under the OMN-17564 remote-leg policy a leg costs min(cores,PREPUSH_REMOTE_XDIST_WORKER_CAP)=min(32,4)=4 xdist workers + 1 idle controller, budgeted at 5.0 runnable cores. Full complement against the 1.0x threshold: 2 slots -> 16.0 (0.50x), 3 -> 21.0 (0.66x), 4 -> 26.0 (0.81x), 5 -> 31.0 (0.97x). 3 is the largest count that still leaves a THIRD of the box (11.0 cores) for what OMN-17485 says must never be starved here: the five live runtime-evidence lanes, the interactive collaborator workspace (OMN-17280), and a returning CI wave -- 90 runners declaring 180 CPUs of ceiling burst past 6 cores the moment work routes back, and at slots=5 that single burst puts the box over 1.0x and lab-host-a then refuses EVERY placement including the lanes already assigned to it. Memory is not binding: the live leg's pytest RSS is 674 MiB, so 3 legs x 5 procs x ~0.7 GiB ~= 10.5 GiB against ~57 GiB MemAvailable and the PREPUSH_MIN_FREE_MEM_MB=4096 floor. slot_mode stays `queue` DELIBERATELY -- the ~/push-lanes/QUEUE serializer is a different mechanism and _PREPUSH_SLOT_PROBE_SH still returns busy on EVERY slot while q!=0, so a non-empty QUEUE collapses this row to zero placements regardless of slot count (OMN-16968/OMN-17419, not this row's business). placement_tier stays `last_resort`: widening slots is not a promotion, this row is still taken only when no default-tier host is fit. Blocked on OMN-17606 to have any effect -- with the unfixed probe one leg reads p=2 held=1 so slot 2 evaluates 2<=1 and refuses; under the merged omnimarket copy (sha256 a591fbdd..., #2276 merged 2026-09-03T00:40:19Z) the same three slots at 11:02:45Z read slot1=BUSY(queue=0 heavy_pids=1 lock=1 held=1) slot2=FREE slot3=FREE.

OMN-17477 RETIRED 2026-09-16: the governed impacted-test selector left pre-push in all three repos (omnibase_infra#3415, omnimarket#2463, omnibase_core#1678), so nothing dispatches a heavy suite to a lab host and this row's slots reserved cores against a leg that no longer runs. Verified rather than taken from the changelog: this repo's .pre-commit-config.yaml carries exactly three pre-push hooks and prepush-smart-tests is not among them. The reservation was not free -- a slot budgets min(cores, PREPUSH_REMOTE_XDIST_WORKER_CAP=4) workers plus a controller, so slots=2 held ten cores, and BOTH Macs now carry self-hosted runners whose capacity plan was double-booking the same cores. Set mode=disabled and slots back to 1 rather than deleting the row: deletion would drop the hostname identity half too, and `disabled` is this table's own documented way to say not probed, not run. Reversible by a reviewed edit plus a deliberate test update, exactly as the promotion that created it was.

OMN-17232: HP ProLiant DL560 Gen8, 80 hardware threads and 377 GiB of memory (free -g on the host read total 377, available 371, 2026-10-30; the lane census figure of 125 GB was wrong). slots=12 holds the memory per concurrent lane at parity with h907: h907 runs 3 slots on 94 GB (31 GB per slot, lab_run_hosts), and 377 GiB over 12 slots is 31.4 GiB per slot (floor of 377 / 31.3); memory and not the 80 threads is the binding resource, so the thread count does not raise it. placement_tier=default ranks this host ahead of h907 (last_resort) for every job it can run. repos_denied is empty: the host has no AVX2 (Ivy Bridge) but no pre-push suite in this repository imports an AVX2 wheel (OMN-17232 census). No remote-leg proof of this repository's suite on this host is recorded in this row; the host is registered unavailable for lab placement, and a probe that cannot reach a host SKIPS it, so the row costs a push nothing until the host answers.
